items.statement: Q1 was the best ever quarter for revenue, BEV revenue and BEV revenue share.
items.quote: So coming to the quarter, I'm happy to share this was the best ever quarter for revenue, BEV revenue, and BEV revenue share, with very healthy momentum, continuing across the business.

items.statement: Revenue grew 54% year on year while EBITDA rose 49% and net profit 45%.
items.quote: Now to the numbers, our revenue grew by 54% year on year, while EBITDA and net profit increased by 49% and 45% respectively.

items.statement: BEV revenue more than doubled, up 107% to Rs 436 crore.
items.quote: BEV revenue grew by 107% to 436 crores over the same quarter last year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin fell about 0.7 points to 23.1%, mainly due to product mix and higher input prices.
items.quote: EBITDA margin was 23.1%, which is lower by about 0.7% compared to the same quarter last year. The margin was lower primarily on account of product mix and higher input prices

items.statement: Value added to employee cost declined because the mix shifted toward assembly products.
items.quote: In case of VA to employee cost, there is a decline compared to previous period, mainly due to change in the product mix in favor of assembly products.

items.statement: Cost recovery measures should become progressively more visible from Q2.
items.quote: We expect that these recovery measures will become progressively more visible from quarter 2 onwards.

items.statement: Management expects phenomenal EV growth this year despite a weak US EV market.
items.quote: But despite that, I think we will see phenomenal, EV growth in the, in this year at least.

items.statement: Demand was healthy in all markets, with India strong in passenger vehicles and electric two-wheelers.
items.quote: Demand has remained healthy across all the markets we serve. India delivered another strong quarter, particularly in passenger vehicles and electric two-wheelers, which was phenomenal.

items.statement: EV sales are limited by OEM supply chains, not by demand.
items.quote: EV is in a way, right now, we are not constrained by demand. Actually, all our OEMs are not constrained by demand. They are constrained by their own supply chain challenges.

items.statement: Cost pass-through to automotive customers lags inflation.
items.quote: Those of you who followed us know that costs pass through with automotive customers always lag inflation, so they come a little later.

items.statement: Inflation in commodities and other inputs remains the biggest near-term challenge and hit margins.
items.quote: Inflation continues to be the biggest near-term challenge. Commodities and other input costs remain elevated. They have impacted margins during the quarter.

items.statement: Margins were hit by input cost inflation, higher labour costs and delayed customer recoveries.
items.quote: Margins were heavily impacted by input cost inflation, labor cost increases as well as the timing gap in the customer recoveries

items.statement: Fast growth in lower-margin traction motors also dragged on margins.
items.quote: There was also a product mix impact as traction motor sales grew quite rapidly, and as is well known to you, that product category has the lowest margins relative to our average company margin

items.statement: Motor and control-system businesses need little capex, about Rs 8-9 of revenue per rupee of capex in two-wheelers.
items.quote: capex intensity of motor business and control system businesses is actually low. I mean, even in our two-wheeler thing, as I think I've shared before, for ₹1 of capex, you can get 8 to 9 rupees of revenue easily

items.statement: The company builds capacity ahead of demand and is not capacity constrained.
items.quote: We have always built capacity ahead of markets and that is definitely not our problem

items.statement: Net order book stands at Rs 240 billion, 64% from EVs.
items.quote: at the end of Q1 FY27, our net order book stands at 240 billion, with EVs accounting for 64%.

items.statement: Two new EV programmes and one hybrid programme took the EV book to 69 programmes across 36 customers.
items.quote: We have also added 2 new EV programs and 1 hybrid program, which takes our EV order book to 69 programs across 36 customers.

items.statement: Three new robotics orders added Rs 6 billion to the Robotics and Physical AI order book.
items.quote: Together, these three orders, they add ₹6 billion to our Robotics and Physical AI orderbook

items.statement: Net debt remains negative, so net debt to EBITDA is also negative.
items.quote: Our net debt continues to be negative. Therefore, net debt to EBITDA ratio also continues in a negative territory.

items.statement: Lower debtor days made this the best quarter for operating cash flow.
items.quote: the working capital turnover ratio also improved due to a significant reduction in debtor days, which also made this as our best quarter from an operational cash flow perspective.

items.statement: Sona Comstar announced a strategic partnership with DENSO, which it calls its most important ever.
items.quote: Yesterday, we announced what I believe is the most important strategic partnership in Sona Comstar's history. A partnership with DENSO.

items.statement: The first DENSO JV covers high-voltage electric and hybrid powertrains for passenger and commercial vehicles.
items.quote: The first will focus on high voltage electric and hybrid powertrain systems for 4 and 4+ wheel vehicles, so all passenger and commercial vehicle applications, in short.

items.statement: The company has already entered Robotics and Physical AI.
items.quote: So we're not announcing our intent to enter Robotics and Physical AI. We're announcing that Sona Comstar has already entered.

items.statement: Europe is electrifying quickly across BEVs, strong hybrids and plug-in hybrids.
items.quote: Europe is electrifying very fast. I mean, whether it be fully BEV or, whether it be strong hybrids or plug-in hybrids, they are actually accelerating quite fast.

items.statement: India is probably the fastest growing EV market in the world.
items.quote: India is actually the fastest growing EV market in the world, I think, right now.

items.statement: The operating environment remains uncertain, with choppy trade and geopolitical developments.
items.quote: Beyond that, the operating environment remains uncertain. We all read the news. Trade and geopolitical developments continue to be choppy.

items.statement: Bottlenecks at other suppliers mean the company sells less than it could.
items.quote: So unfortunately, we are able to sell less than we ideally would have, but not much we can do about other players in the supply chain.

items.statement: Heavy rare earth magnet imports remain restricted, so the company uses light rare earth alternatives.
items.quote: rare earth magnets are still restricted. So heavy rare earth magnets cannot be imported. Almost all that we do today is with light rare earth alternatives, and it's working fine.

items.statement: positive
items.quote: So coming to the quarter, I'm happy to share this was the best ever quarter for revenue, BEV revenue, and BEV revenue share, with very healthy momentum, continuing across the business.

items.statement: Revenue grew 35% year on year while EBITDA and net profit rose 23% and 29%.
items.quote: revenue grew 35% year on year. While EBITDA and net profit increased by 23% in 29% respectively.

items.statement: BEV revenue grew 129% year on year and for the first time exceeded half of automotive revenue.
items.quote: Turning to BEVs, we continue to see electrification growth, with growth accelerating to 129%, year on year. For the first time, BEVs contribute more than 50% of our automotive revenue.

items.statement: The company generated its highest ever free cash flow from operations.
items.quote: We delivered our highest ever free cash flow from operations. In just six months of this year, we have generated more than $1.5 times the FCFO we generated in the entire FY26.

items.statement: EBITDA margin fell 2.3 percentage points year on year to 23% due to product mix and higher input prices.
items.quote: EBITDA margin was 23%, which was lower by 2.3% compared to the same quarter last year. The margin was lower primarily on account of change in the product mix and higher input prices

items.statement: The VA to employee cost ratio declined due to a product mix shift toward assembly products.
items.quote: In case of VA to employee cost the ratio there is a decline compared to previous period mainly due to change in the product mix in favor of assembly products.

items.statement: The West Asia war is pushing up steel, copper and oil derivative costs, and freight rates nearly doubled.
items.quote: The war invest Asia continues to add to cost pressures with the further increases in steel, copper, and oil derivatives. Freight rates have also risen sharply. they've nearly doubled from previous quarter's level.

items.statement: Strong growth and operating leverage helped absorb most cost pressures and hold margins.
items.quote: Strong growth and better operating leverage is what has helped us absorb most of these pressures and continue to at least hold the line on margins.

items.statement: Pass-through of material costs happens with a lag, so margins dip when prices rise.
items.quote: there is a pass-through mechanism with the customers that but there will be a lead lag effect essentially so the prices will go up fast and then with the lag the prices get passed on to the customers

items.statement: Management sees no reason to change its 23-25% EBITDA margin range.
items.quote: I don't think there is any reason to change our range I think 23 to 25 is fair we are genuinely in exceptional inflation at this point

items.statement: The company's aspiration implies a 25% CAGR, which it expects to sustain in the medium term.
items.quote: we have already given our aspiration which actually does imply a 25 CAGR

items.statement: Mix shift toward traction motors and uncertain West Asia inflation make near-term predictability difficult.
items.quote: Looking ahead, stronger traction motor demand is changing our mix. And broader inflation linked to West Asia remains uncertain. Both these factors are largely beyond our control. which makes near-term predictability a little difficult.

items.statement: Return ratios improved and are expected to keep improving.
items.quote: Our return ratios have also improved, and we expect them to continue improving.

items.statement: Traction motor demand exceeded internal expectations, growing almost 50% quarter on quarter.
items.quote: Traction motor demand has significantly exceeded even our own internal expectations. the business has grown almost 50% quarter on quarter.

items.statement: EV demand is accelerating, led by electric two- and three-wheelers in India.
items.quote: demand for EVs continues to accelerate. EV business grew by an almost unbelievable, 129% year on year. In India, strong demand for electric 2 and 3 wheelers was the biggest reason.

items.statement: The company won Rs 36 billion of new business, its third highest quarter for order additions.
items.quote: if you look at the pro quarter as a whole, we won 36 billion worth of new business, which is the third highest quarter for order additions.

items.statement: The net order book stood at Rs 251 billion at the end of Q2.
items.quote: thanks to that, we have closed Q2 with a net order book of 251 billion.

items.statement: Three new products were commercialised: a helical limited slip differential, railway air springs and rear radar sensors for two-wheelers.
items.quote: We've introduced a helical limited slip differential, air springs for railways, and rear radar sensors for two wheelers.

items.statement: The first strategic priority was broadened from electrification to EPIC mobility.
items.quote: We are broadening our first priority from electrification to epic mobility. For the sake of repetition, this stands for electric personalized intelligent and connected solutions.

items.statement: The company targets closing the Denso JV1 carve-out by end of December, possibly slipping into January.
items.quote: we are targeting to close this by at least the JV1 part of it which is carving out of the business by end of December

items.statement: The company held Rs 1,966 crore in cash and investments at end of September, with negative net debt to EBITDA.
items.quote: Consequent to all these movements as of end of September we had cash and investments worth 1,966 crores.

items.statement: H1 capex of about Rs 148 crore left free cash flow of Rs 446 crore.
items.quote: Net of capex spend of about 148 crores we generated 446 crores of free cash flows which was more than 50% higher than what we generated in the last full financial year.

items.statement: Rs 62 crore of capex has been earmarked for the robotics and physical AI area.
items.quote: the capex as you know we had declared last quarter I think that 62 crore of capex is for this area that should cover it

items.statement: European OEMs seeking alternatives to China supply chains are giving the company more business in Europe.
items.quote: Europe we are winning more business and we're seeing a lot more traction as a lot of European OEMs want to have an alternative supply chain to China

items.statement: Margins would deteriorate only if material prices keep rising further.
items.quote: the only scenario where it deteriorates is if the material prices can continue to inch higher that also seems improbable because beyond a point things start to break down

items.statement: China's export restrictions on heavy rare earth materials continue, with no sign of easing.
items.quote: the restrictions on export of heavy rare earth materials from China continue so in that scenario it is not possible

items.statement: positive
items.quote: Q2 was almost a perfect quarter for us across all metrics. financial performance, new order wins, technology and new products, cash flow generation, and our total quality management.

items.statement: The company delivered record revenue, EBITDA and PAT, and BEV revenue exceeded half of automotive revenue for the first time.
items.quote: We delivered our highest ever revenue, EBITDA and PAT. BEV revenue also reached an all-time high, and for the first time, contributed more than half of our automotive revenue.

items.statement: Quarterly revenue grew 35% year on year to Rs 1,546 crore.
items.quote: First, the quarter's results, our revenue for the quarter grew by 35% year on year to ₹1,546 crore.

items.statement: Free cash flow from operations hit a record, with six months already exceeding 1.5 times FY26's total.
items.quote: We delivered our highest ever free cash flow from operations. In just 6 months of this year, we have generated more than 1.5 times the FCFO we generated in the entire FY26.

items.statement: The VA to employee cost ratio declined due to a product mix shift toward assembly products.
items.quote: In case of VA to employee cost, the ratio, there is a decline compared to previous period, mainly due to change in the product mix in favor of assembly products.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 23%, down 2.3 points year on year, due to product mix and higher input prices.
items.quote: EBITDA margin was 23%, which was lower by 2.3% compared to the same quarter last year. The margin was lower primarily on account of change in the product mix and higher input prices.

items.statement: Margin pressure continued this quarter mainly due to product mix as traction motor demand exceeded expectations.
items.quote: this quarter, the continued margin pressure has been there, but it's mainly driven by change in product mix. Traction motor demand has significantly exceeded even our own internal expectations.

items.statement: If material prices stay flat, the company expects to hold margins as pass-through catches up.
items.quote: Material prices if they continue to be this high if they are flattish I think we should be able to hold on to this margin

items.statement: The West Asia war is raising steel, copper and oil derivative costs, and freight rates nearly doubled quarter on quarter.
items.quote: The war in West Asia continues to cause pressures with further increases in steel, copper, and oil derivatives. Freight rates have also risen sharply, they've nearly doubled from the previous quarter's level.

items.statement: Going forward, traction motor demand is shifting the mix and West Asia-linked inflation remains uncertain.
items.quote: Looking ahead, stronger traction motor demand is changing our mix and broader inflation linked to West Asia remains uncertain.

items.statement: Management sees no reason to change its 23-25% EBITDA margin range.
items.quote: I don't think there is any reason to change our range, I think 23-25 is fair.

items.statement: The company's stated aspiration implies a 25% revenue CAGR.
items.quote: Pamod, in short we've already given our aspiration which actually does imply a 25% CAGR.

items.statement: EV demand is accelerating, with the EV business up 129% year on year, led by Indian electric 2- and 3-wheelers.
items.quote: Demand for EVs continues to accelerate. Our EV business grew by almost unbelievable 129% year on year. In India, strong demand for electric 2 and 3 wheelers was the biggest reason.

items.statement: The company won Rs 36 billion of new business, its third-highest quarter for order additions.
items.quote: So if you look at the quarter as a whole, we won 36 billion worth of new business, which is the 3rd highest quarter for order additions.

items.statement: The net order book stood at Rs 251 billion at the end of Q2.
items.quote: And thanks to that, we have closed Q2 with a net order book of 251 billion.

items.statement: Cash and investments stood at Rs 1,966 crore at the end of September.
items.quote: Consequent to all these movements, as of end of September we had cash and investments worth 1,966 crores.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA remains negative.
items.quote: Net debt to ebitda ratio continues to be in the negative territory for obvious reasons.

items.statement: Capex of about Rs 148 crore in H1 still left Rs 446 crore of free cash flow.
items.quote: Net of capex spend of about 148 crores. We generated 446 crores of free cash flows

items.statement: Rs 62 crore of previously announced capex is allocated to robotics and physical AI.
items.quote: the capex as you know we had declared last quarter I think that 62 crore of capex is for this area.

items.statement: Three new products were launched: a helical limited slip differential, railway air springs and two-wheeler rear radar sensors.
items.quote: We've introduced a helical limited slip differential, air springs for railways, and rear radar sensors for two-wheelers

items.statement: The company targets closing the first Denso JV carve-out by end of December.
items.quote: So we're targeting to close this JV 1 part of it which is carving out of the business by end of December

items.statement: The company has the capability and spare capacity to ramp up production quickly.
items.quote: We have the capability and the capacity available to do that with agility.

items.statement: European OEMs want alternative supply chains to China, which is bringing the company more business in Europe.
items.quote: in Europe we are gaining more business and we’re seeing a lot more traction as a lot of European OEMs want to have an alternative supply chain to China

items.statement: China's export restrictions on heavy rare earth materials continue, preventing their use.
items.quote: the restrictions on export of heavy rare earth materials from China continue, so in that scenario it is not possible

items.statement: Management expects margins to hold unless oil reaches 150.
items.quote: Basu, in short, unless oil goes to 150 when all bets are off, we think we will hold.

items.statement: positive
items.quote: Q2 was almost a perfect quarter for us across all metrics- financial performance, new order wins, technology and new products, cash flow generation, and our total quality management.
